summary: With App Control enabled some modules behave differently: win_command and win_package only run trusted executables, win_shell runs in Constrained Language Mode, win_powershell and script run in CLM unless the script is signed, and win_updates doesn't work. Signed scripts must not be modified, including line endings and whitespace.
questions: Does win_updates work with Windows App Control enabled?

How can I make win_powershell run in Full Language mode under WDAC?

How do I check the PowerShell language mode from Ansible?

answer_card.title: Module behaviour with Windows App Control
answer_card.answer_md:
Known differences when App Control is enabled (even with signing):
- `win_command` only runs executables trusted by the policy.
- `win_shell` always runs in Constrained Language Mode (CLM), which may break scripts.
- `win_powershell` and `ansible.builtin.script` run in CLM unless the script is signed.
- `win_package` only runs trusted executables, so it may or may not work.
- `win_updates` is not supported.

Other modules that start sub-processes or rely on unsigned PowerShell will most likely fail.

Check the language mode:

```yaml
- name: Test out LanguageMode
  ansible.windows.win_powershell:
    script: $ExecutionContext.SessionState.LanguageMode
```

A signed script must be used exactly as signed, with the same line endings and whitespace.
